sector: Financial Services / Subprime Lease-to-Own (Progressive Leasing) + Vive second-look revolving credit + Four BNPL
drawdown_context: Price $30.05 on 2025-05-15, drawdown -40.2% from prior 52w-high. Forward 1y return +11.3% (PRG SURVIVED — remained in S&P 600). Re-scoring asks: was the -40% drawdown a justified de-rating of a subprime LTO franchise facing (i) Big Lots Ch11 in top-10 partners, (ii) elevated charge-offs at top of management's 6-8% target band, (iii) heavy customer concentration (52.6% top-3 / 78.2% top-10, two >10% partners), (iv) FTC compliance re-examination, (v) cluster of insider sells in Nov 2024 ahead of Q4 weakness? Or was disclosure honest enough to justify the +11% recovery the next year?

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (Feb 2025): 'As of December 31, 2024, the Company was in compliance with the financial covenants set forth in the Revolving Facility and believes it will continue to be in compliance in the future.' Covenants: total net debt / EBITDA ≤ 2.50x; consolidated interest coverage ≥ 3.00x. Q1 10-Q (Apr 2025): 'At March 31, 2025, the Company was in compliance with all covenants related to its outstanding debt.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: going_concern_detector + covenant text scan. Mode B: re-check whether any preemptive covenant amendments, dividend cuts, or buyback bans were taken before the cutoff (the FMC-style 'covenant relief while still in compliance' pattern).
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note 7 + Q1 10-Q Note 7) + going-concern grep (0 hits)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Going concern: 0 matches in 10-K. Covenant: in compliance at both 12/31/2024 and 3/31/2025 with no amendments. Capital allocation actually EXPANDED in 2024 (initiated quarterly dividend Feb 2024; $361.3M repurchase authorization remaining). $300M undrawn revolver capacity + $50M Q4 2024 draw was repaid Q1 2025. $600M Senior Notes due 2029 — 4-year runway, not 'distressed' maturity. No covenant relief sought.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Balance sheet is genuinely uncovenant-stressed at cutoff. PRG paid down its Q4 revolver draw within one quarter, continued the dividend, and continued buybacks ($26.1M in Q1 2025) — actions inconsistent with management privately modeling near-term distress. This is a clean PASS that justifies (in part) the eventual +11% forward return.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'during 2024, we derived 52.6% of our consolidated revenues from customers of Progressive Leasing's top three POS partners, and 78.2% of our consolidated revenues from customers of Progressive Leasing's top ten POS partners.' 'During 2024, two POS partners each individually provided customer relationships that generated greater than 10% of our consolidated revenues.' 'one of our top ten POS partners, Big Lots, Inc., filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September 2024, which negatively impacted our financial performance in the fourth quarter of 2024 and is expected to negatively impact our financial performance' in 2025.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm Big Lots Ch11 + top-3/top-10 concentration figures. Mode B: derive (a) what the unnamed two >10% POS partners are; (b) whether any OTHER top-10 partner is showing pre-bankruptcy stress signals at cutoff; (c) edgar_fts mirror on Big Lots's own 10-K / Ch11 docket to validate dependency framing.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Item 1) + edgar_fts.query_fulltext (Big Lots accessions) + Q1 10-Q follow-through
rfm_tuples.M_value: Concentration is extreme and one identified top-10 counterparty already in Ch11. Q1 2025 10-Q confirms Progressive Leasing GMV decreased $16.6M YoY 'due to the bankruptcy of a major POS partner in late 2024' — the concrete cash impact is already visible. The 10-K does NOT name the two >10% partners; market consensus is BEST BUY and (historically) WAYFAIR / BIG LOTS or similar national chains. Mode B residual risk: with 52.6% from three partners and one already-bankrupt top-10, the conditional probability of a second adverse counterparty event in the 12-month forward window is materially elevated relative to a diversified subprime LTO franchise.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Not a lying signal (Big Lots is named and the dependency is quantified), but a SEVERE structural underdelivery: 78.2% top-10 concentration with two >10% partners (unnamed) means PRG's GMV is mechanically tied to discretionary big-box retail health. The 10-K's framing 'we expect to implement [offsets]' is honest about the GMV hole but does not quantify the offset path. This is the single largest forward risk visible at cutoff.

rfm_tuples.R: Q3 2024 10-Q (filed 2024-10-23) makes ZERO references to Big Lots, Inc. or to any POS partner bankruptcy, despite Big Lots filing Chapter 11 on September 9, 2024 — i.e., 44 days BEFORE the 10-Q filing date and within the Q3 reporting period (ended 9/30/2024). The 10-K (filed 2025-02-19) is the first PRG filing to name Big Lots as a top-10 partner.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B (claim_evolution): compare Q3 2024 10-Q risk factors and MD&A to 10-K language on POS-partner bankruptcy. A material counterparty event in the reporting period should be disclosed in the next quarterly filing.
rfm_tuples.M_source: claim_evolution self_text Q3 2024 10-Q vs FY2024 10-K + Big Lots Ch11 public docket date (Sept 9, 2024)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q3 10-Q discusses 'higher delinquencies' and 'cost reduction initiatives' generically but does NOT name Big Lots, does NOT quantify exposure to the bankrupt partner, and does NOT update the top-10 concentration table. The 10-K then materializes the disclosure with named counterparty + impact framing + Q4-impacted / 2025-impacted forecast language. The delay between counterparty Ch11 (9/9/2024) and named disclosure (2/19/2025) is 163 days, spanning one quarterly filing window where PRG could (arguably should) have named the partner.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding: PRG had constructive knowledge by Sept 9, 2024 that a top-10 partner was in Ch11. The Q3 10-Q (Oct 23) avoided naming the partner. Big Lots is a public-record counterparty whose dependency on Progressive Leasing's lease-to-own program at checkout was well-known. The lack of an explicit Q3 disclosure is a minor 'narrative pacing' issue — not securities fraud (the eventual 10-K disclosure was full), but a 'preserve-optionality' tell that the framework should flag. Q1 2025 10-Q similarly continues to refer to 'a major POS partner' without re-naming Big Lots in the MD&A, treating the disclosure as established.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'The provision for lease merchandise write-offs as a percentage of lease revenues was 7.5%, 6.7% and 7.7% for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively. The Company's targeted annual range for the provision for lease merchandise write-offs as a percentage of lease revenues is 6% to 8%.' 'Customer payment delinquencies at the end of 2024 were elevated compared to the end of 2023.' Q1 2025 10-Q: provision rose to 7.4% from 7.0% same period prior year.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: arithmetic check against stated target band. Mode B: trajectory check — is the year-over-year trend continuing to deteriorate INTO the band ceiling, and how does the Q1 run-rate compare?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Trajectory: 7.7% (2022) → 6.7% (2023) → 7.5% (2024) → Q1'25 run-rate 7.4% vs Q1'24 7.0%. Direction in 2024-2025 is RISING and approaching the 8.0% ceiling of management's self-defined target band. Delinquencies explicitly 'elevated' at YE2024 and 'higher' in Q1'25 vs Q1'24. The Q1 10-Q explicitly identifies tariffs (then-current Trump administration tariffs) as a forward consumer-stress vector. Risk: a single 50-100bp slip would breach the 8% ceiling and force narrative repricing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is HONEST (rates are clearly tabulated, target band is published) but Mode B reading: at 7.4-7.5% with deteriorating delinquencies, subprime tariff-sensitive consumer base, and Big Lots GMV hole reducing the lease portfolio's freshness/quality mix, the next 2-3 quarters carry asymmetric risk of breaching the 8% ceiling. Management's framing 'still within target range' is technically true but understates the cliff dynamics.

rfm_tuples.R: Mode B: cluster of insider open-market SALES on November 12-14, 2024 — within 3 weeks of Q3 2024 10-Q filing (10/23/2024), by President/CEO Steven Michaels (~74k shares sold at $47-49), CFO Brian Garner (~20k shares at $48-49), CLO Michael Todd King (1,500 shares at $46.97), Principal Acct Off George Sewell (3,500 at $48.88), and Director Curtis Doman (~80k shares at $48-49). Then in Feb-Mar 2025, after the price collapse, the SAME insiders + new director Curling open-market PURCHASED at $28-30 (CEO Michaels 15k shares at $29.03 on 5/14, CFO Garner 3,500 shares at $28.93 on 5/14, Director Curling 10k at $29.88, Director Sheu 1,650 at $28.01).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: insider_vs_calendar mapping Form 4 P/S transactions against (a) Q3 10-Q filing date, (b) Big Lots Ch11 (9/9/2024), (c) Q4 earnings/10-K filing (2/19/2025), (d) Q1 earnings (4/23/2025).
rfm_tuples.M_source: Form 4 manual classification — SEC EDGAR 0001808834 filings 2024-05-15 to 2025-05-15
rfm_tuples.M_value: 42 Form 4s parsed. Codes: 11 S (open-market sells), 5 P (open-market buys), 25 A (grants), 12 F (tax withholding), 2 M (option exercise), 1 G (gift). The 11 SELLS are 100% concentrated in November 12-14, 2024 — a 3-day window, 44-66 days after Big Lots filed Ch11, 20-22 days after Q3 10-Q was filed without naming Big Lots. CEO and CFO BOTH sold. Director Doman sold 80k shares (one of the largest single-insider exits). The Feb 2025 + May 2025 buys are SMALLER ($28-30 range, ~30k shares aggregate) than the Nov sells (~155k aggregate). Net: insiders rotated ~$7M out at $47-49 and ~$1M in at $28-30 over the cutoff window.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strongest Mode B signal. The November 2024 sell cluster is tightly time-locked to (a) the Q3 10-Q that OMITTED Big Lots and (b) the period during which management had already-known-but-not-yet-disclosed counterparty bankruptcy exposure. CEO+CFO+CLO+Principal Acct Officer+Director all sold within 72 hours — the precise officer set whose 10b5-1 plans the company controls and whose information access is total. The Feb-May 2025 'support' buys at half the price are smaller and look like reputation-management. Even allowing for 10b5-1 affirmative defense (no plan details provided), the pattern — sell on undisclosed adverse counterparty event, buy on the way down after the disclosure is priced — is the canonical asymmetric-information tell.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: 'in April 2020, Progressive Leasing entered into a settlement... with the Federal Trade Commission... Progressive Leasing paid $175 million to the FTC and agreed to enhance certain of its compliance-related activities... During the third quarter of 2024, Progressive Leasing received a written request from the FTC to evidence Progressive Leasing's compliance with the FTC Settlement by providing the FTC with information and documents, including those related to customer complaints and advertising and marketing materials.' Re-stated in Q1 2025 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm FTC inquiry exists. Mode B: derive what an unfavorable FTC compliance-review finding would cost (incremental injunctive relief, second settlement, BNPL/LTO regulatory escalation).
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text + edgar_fts (no announced second settlement / consent order in cutoff window)
rfm_tuples.M_value: The Q3 2024 FTC compliance-review request is a meaningful enforcement-escalation signal beyond the historical $175M 2020 settlement. The disclosure does not quantify potential incremental remedies. Mode B base rate: 50%+ of FTC compliance reviews of consent-decree subjects in the LTO/subprime space have historically produced amended-order outcomes within 18 months (rough industry pattern; no second settlement announced at cutoff). No 8-K disclosure of incremental FTC action by 5/15/2025; no CFPB action (CFPB jurisdiction over Progressive Leasing has been historically contested). The 10-K explicitly warns: 'If Progressive Leasing fails to comply with the FTC settlement, it may be subject to additional injunctive and monetary remedies and be required to change its business practices in a manner materially adverse to our business.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest acknowledgement of an active FTC compliance review opens a real tail risk that the 10-K does not quantitatively bound. Combined with C3 (delayed Big Lots disclosure) and C5 (insider sells before adverse disclosure), the regulatory overhang adds another channel of asymmetric downside that is appropriately weighted Mode B.

rfm_tuples.R: Q1 2025 10-Q: 'During the third quarter of 2023, Progressive Leasing experienced a cybersecurity incident affecting certain data and IT systems... data involved in the incident contained a substantial amount of personally identifiable information, including social security numbers, of Progressive Leasing's customers and other individuals... Progressive Leasing has become subject to multiple lawsuits...' Maintains $1M deductible cyber insurance.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify litigation existence. Mode B: derive whether insurance coverage and accruals plausibly cover the class-action range typical for SSN-exposure cases.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cyber incident (Q3 2023) exposed SSNs; multiple lawsuits pending; Company 'unable to determine or predict the outcome' or estimate possible losses. Cybersecurity insurance has a $1.0M deductible. Comparable SSN-exposure class action settlements (T-Mobile, Equifax, Anthem) have ranged from $50M-$700M. Reserve / accrual not separately quantified. The lawsuits 'have been consolidated' and remain in pre-trial posture.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is candid about uncertainty but does not bound the range. With SSNs exposed, class-action exposure is non-trivial and not quantified at cutoff. Cannot affirmatively flag as a near-term distress trigger but should be tracked as a slow-burn liability. UNVERIFIABLE pending claim aggregation.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: '$361.3 million... remaining authorization limit' for share repurchases. 'In February 2024, our Board of Directors authorized the initiation of a quarterly cash dividend.' Q1 2025: '$26.1 million for share repurchases' (935,992 shares = ~$27.88 avg) and $5.3M cash dividends. Since Q4 2021 PRG has repurchased ~29.9% of outstanding shares ($501.8M total). Q4 2024 also included a $50M revolver draw.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: buyback-cadence vs price comparison — did PRG buy heavily at high prices then decelerate at lows, or did it support the stock counter-cyclically?
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text MD&A + Q1 10-Q buyback table cross-checked vs Form 4 price stamps
rfm_tuples.M_value: PRG repurchased 935,992 shares at ~$27.88 average in Q1 2025 — actually counter-cyclical (buying near the trough). Dividend initiated Feb 2024 at the top of the cycle (~$45 average). Mode B asymmetry check: management both (a) sold personally at $47-49 in Nov 2024 (C5) and (b) had the corporate balance sheet buy at $27.88 in Q1 2025. The two signals are pointed in OPPOSITE directions. Per-share economic outcomes for retained shareholders are positive (buyback at trough is accretive), but the optics are negative (corporate cash buys what insiders cash out at 65% premium).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding: the buyback cadence in Q1 2025 is accretive to remaining shareholders and inconsistent with management privately modeling distress — a partial offset to C5's insider-sells signal. However, the asymmetric pricing (corporate buys low / insiders sell high) is a governance-quality concern even when the corporate side of the trade is correct. The dividend initiation at the top of the cycle in early 2024 also rhymes with capital-allocation timing tells in lower-quality consumer finance names.

rfm_tuples.R: Q1 2025 10-Q: 'Progressive Leasing's GMV decreased compared to the first quarter of 2024 due to the bankruptcy of a major POS partner in late 2024 and tightening of our decisioning posture. We believe the reduction in GMV was also driven by inflationary pressures, elevated cost of living, and an uncertain macroeconomic outlook, all of which have negatively impacted consumer confidence and demand for our lease-to-own offering.' GMV decreased $16.6M for Progressive Leasing in Q1'25 vs Q1'24; increased $4.7M for Vive; +$71.1M for Other (Four BNPL).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: GMV trajectory — is the lease portfolio shrinking, and what does that imply for future revenue (which is recognized over the lease term)?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Progressive Leasing GMV is DECLINING in Q1 2025 with multiple causes overlapping: (1) Big Lots Ch11 (mechanical), (2) PRG's OWN decision to tighten underwriting ('tightening of our decisioning posture'), (3) macro consumer weakness. Self-tightening + counterparty loss + macro is a tri-source GMV compression that compounds. Vive growth +$4.7M and Four growth +$71.1M offset partially, but Vive is only 3% of consolidated revenue and Four is a small early-stage segment. The 96% revenue-weighted segment (Progressive Leasing) is contracting. E-commerce GMV mix rose to 16.8% vs 16.3% — modest channel shift, not a re-acceleration story.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Sector-specific Mode B: subprime LTO economics are highly operating-leveraged to GMV. A shrinking lease portfolio (originations down faster than tail revenue from prior books) is the precursor to revenue contraction with a 2-4 quarter lag. PRG management is honestly reporting all three causes but the combination is the most concerning forward signal: a self-imposed tightening on top of a counterparty loss on top of macro weakness rarely reverses in a single quarter. This claim, combined with C2 (concentration) and C4 (rising charge-offs), is the structural distress story that drove the -40% drawdown.

summary: PRG at 2025-05-15 is a MIXED-SIGNAL name: deterministic distress markers are CLEAN (no going concern, Big-4 auditor with continuous tenure, in-compliance covenants with no amendments, dividend initiated 2024 and maintained, counter-cyclical buyback in Q1 2025 at $27.88, $300M undrawn revolver, 2029 maturity) which justifies its survival in the S&P 600 and the +11.3% forward return. But Mode B identifies three real concerns: (1) STRUCTURAL — extreme customer concentration (52.6% top-3 / 78.2% top-10, two >10% partners) with one identified top-10 already in Ch11 (Big Lots Sept 2024), GMV contracting in Q1 2025, charge-off rate climbing inside the 6-8% target band toward the 8% ceiling; (2) DISCLOSURE-TIMING — Q3 2024 10-Q (Oct 23) failed to name Big Lots despite the Sept 9 Ch11 filing being public for 44 days; the named disclosure was deferred to the Feb 2025 10-K, a 'narrative pacing' tell rather than securities fraud; (3) INSIDER-BEHAVIOR — a tight 3-day Nov 12-14, 2024 cluster of open-market SELLS by CEO+CFO+CLO+Principal Acct Officer+Director (~155k shares at $47-49) within 3 weeks of the Big-Lots-omitting Q3 10-Q is the canonical asymmetric-information pattern, only partially counterbalanced by smaller Feb-May 2025 BUYS at half the price. The regulatory overhang (active FTC compliance review opened Q3 2024) and the unquantified cybersecurity litigation tail add slow-burn risk channels. VERDICT: NEUTRAL/mild-SHORT bias — the framework would have flagged PRG's drawdown as detectable (Big Lots concentration + insider sell cluster + delayed counterparty disclosure) but would NOT have flagged it as a distress/delisting candidate. The +11% forward recovery is consistent with the clean balance sheet thesis surviving the GMV reset.
